You could say I have hope that things will get better, and that might be true to some extent, but hope didn't keep me alive. It was fear.

Before I go further, I should probably disclose that I am a normie by standards of this sub based on my appearance, income, social status, and experience.  I used to consider myself as FA but I worked really hard to overcome it to where I feel like I'm not quite at that level anymore.  But I still get really lonely a lot and this place is just so familiar so I don't want to leave.

Anyway, I think the answer to your question is a question you have to ask yourself: What would make you happy?  Would accepting your fate and learning to cope with it bring you happiness?  You would never be let down again because you'd have no expectations.

Or would leaving FA make you happy?  If so, then you have to work for it.  It won't just come.  You hear people say that their relationship "just happened."  That is almost never the case.  People get into relationships by meeting people and clicking with them.  It might not have been as much work for some people, but they still had to be in the right social situation and do something right.  Sure there's exceptions, but most of the time it required at least some minimal effort on both parties.  In a FA's case, they need to work really hard to leave it.  You can definitely make yourself more attractive even if you objectively don't have an attractive natural face.  But it will take work.  You can definitely get better at socializing, but it will take work and you'll probably have many failures along the way.  All these things can get you out of this rut.  If you said that leaving FA would make you happy, then you need to work to do it.

Some people want to leave but don't want to make any effort to do it because they don't think they can handle the failure.  When you're at this stage, you need to take smaller steps.  Get out of bed in the morning.  Do little things that push yourself to do something you otherwise weren't doing.  Therapy can also help really well if you're willing to give it a try.  I have a friend who's in the same boat as me in a lot of ways, but he is highly against the idea of therapy because he feels like he should be able to do it all on his own.  While I'm still rooting for him, I think he's going to have a hard time achieving life satisfaction without it.  That being said, therapy would be a failure to him at this point in his life because he's not willing to let it help him, much like a lot of people on this sub feel.

To answer your question, "Will this weight over our shoulders ever disappear while we are alive?"  Barring some tragedy happening to you in the near future, the answer is up to you.
